title: Runboard: compact per-session tracker
content:
Purpose: quick personal runboard to log small inference experiments (latency/cost tradeoffs). Lightweight: use during local sessions or quick remote runs. Not official metrics — ad-hoc and noisy.

Table (CSV-like):
run_id, date, model, quant, batch_size, seq_len, tokens_out, p50_ms, p95_ms, cost_per_1k_tokens_usd, notes
R-2026-03-08-01, 2026-03-08, gptx-small-v1, 8-bit, 1, 32, 128, 42, 110, 0.018, baseline, no prefix cache
R-2026-03-08-02, 2026-03-08, gptx-small-v1, 8-bit, 8, 32, 128, 48, 130, 0.012, batching helped tail, slight quality check
R-2026-03-09-01, 2026-03-09, gptx-medium-v1, 4-bit, 1, 64, 256, 95, 320, 0.045, medium model single-shot
R-2026-03-09-03, 2026-03-09, gptx-medium-v1, 4-bit, 4, 64, 256, 110, 360, 0.033, activate KV-prefix cache -> p50 down 20%
R-2026-03-10-01, 2026-03-10, gptx-small-v1, 8-bit, 16, 32, 128, 62, 180, 0.009, high-batch, saw occasional stall (GC?)
R-2026-03-11-01, 2026-03-11, gptx-small-v1, fp16, 8, 32, 128, 38, 100, 0.025, fp16 slightly faster p50, cost higher per-token

Quick observations (notes-to-self):
- Batching reduces unit cost as expected, but p95 increases nonlinearly beyond batch=8 for small model on this infra. Suspect scheduler/queue overflow at bursts.
- KV-prefix caching gives consistent p50 improvements on medium model; need to quantify hit rates (add explicit hit/miss logging).
- 4-bit quant reduces memory and enables larger batch, but p95 tails worse than 8-bit for same batch sizes (investigate kernel choice).
- fp16 gives best p50 but cost per token higher due to model footprint and licensing? (confirm accounting formula).
- Occasional stall observed at high-batch on 2026-03-10 run — check SLI CPU steal / node swap logs.

Short commands used (for reproducibility):
- curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"model":"gptx-small-v1","input":"<prompt>","batch":8}'
- locally: ./runner --model gptx-medium-v1 --quant 4bit --batch 4 --seq 64 --log perf.json

Next steps / TODOs:
- Add a tiny script to compute cost_per_1k automatically from perf.json (TODO: assign to @Devon).
- Instrument KV cache hit/miss logging on canary nodes (file ticket INF-344).
- Re-run medium-model with kernel override (experiment: use matmul-optimized kernel v2) and record p95.
- Short post-mortem for 2026-03-10 stall: collect node metrics, attach to this doc.

Open questions:
- Are accounting rates used in cost_per_1k the right ones? cross-check with finance published pricing (link?).
- Does batch-induced tail scale linearly with queue depth or are there nonlinear scheduling artifacts? Need controlled microbench.

Quick summary line (for Slack):
"Runboard: batching saves cost but increases p95 after batch>8 on small model; KV cache helps p50 on medium model. Will instrument cache hitrates and rerun kernels next week."

Context links:
- Slack: #perf-quick (thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C02PERF123/p1679990000000)
- PR: gh:.../pr-482 (kernel selection hooks)

Random notes / brain-dump:
- Could consider tiny adaptive-batch policy: start batch=1 and opportunistically increase if queue empty for X ms. Worth prototyping in runner.
- When logging, attach full prompt length distribution, not just seq_len — tail often due to few long prompts.

End of sheet (scratch).
